AndroidTestingRules.keywords: android, testing, junit4, junit5, robolectric, androidx-test, kotlin, gradle
AndroidTestingRules.Mission:
Canonical baseline for testing Android/Kotlin projects: local unit tests on JVM (JUnit4/JUnit5), instrumented tests under `src/androidTest/**` (AndroidX Test), and Robolectric bridges when a JVM unit test genuinely needs Android SDK primitives. Every execution-agent MUST place tests in the correct source set, avoid the `Local test lies about Android runtime` foot-gun, and treat instrumented tests as out-of-scope for the SDD verify loop (no emulator/device in `gennady verify`; that class of test is CI-only or `extraGates`).
**Base axiom:** the Android source-set layout (`src/test/` vs `src/androidTest/`) is a contract, not a suggestion. A local test that imports `android.content.Context` and mocks it convinces the reviewer of a runtime property it never actually verified. Discipline: local unit = pure JVM, no Android framework classes; instrumented = real device/emulator via AndroidX Test; Robolectric = JVM with real Android framework classes when the tested contract requires them.
Scope: JUnit4/JUnit5-based `src/test/**` (local unit) + `src/androidTest/**` (instrumented) + Robolectric. Out of scope: Jetpack Compose UI test, Paparazzi screenshot, Espresso interaction — separate directives to be layered on top later.

BeliefState.Axiom: Test source set is not a stylistic choice — it changes what runs and where. `src/test/java` and `src/test/kotlin` run on the developer's JVM through the `testDebugUnitTest` Gradle task (fast, in-process, no Android framework unless Robolectric is present). `src/androidTest/java` and `src/androidTest/kotlin` run on a real device or emulator through the `connectedAndroidTest` task (slow, real Android runtime). Putting an instrumented test in `src/test/` produces a `NoClassDefFoundError` or a silent stub call at runtime; putting a pure JVM test in `src/androidTest/` wastes device time and blocks CI.

A local unit test in `src/test/**` MUST NOT import `android.*` classes directly, and MUST NOT mock them with `mockito`/`mockk` to pretend the framework is present. If the test genuinely needs an Android framework class, the correct answer is one of: (a) refactor production code so the framework dependency is injected as an interface with a JVM stub in tests; (b) move the test to `src/androidTest/**`; (c) use Robolectric explicitly (AX_ANDROID_TEST_ROBOLECTRIC_OPT_IN). Mocking the framework in a local test is a lie about the runtime.

`connectedAndroidTest` is deliberately excluded from `gennady verify` base plan (D-STACK-015): it requires an emulator/device, orthogonal to the SDD execute→verify inner loop. Instrumented tests are authored under `src/androidTest/**` and executed in CI or manually; if a project needs them in the local loop for a specific pipeline, declare via `stack.android.extraGates` — not by moving instrumented tests into `src/test/`.

Robolectric provides Android framework classes on the JVM. Use it only when the tested contract genuinely involves Android primitives (SharedPreferences behavior, Resources parsing, a Fragment lifecycle) AND running on device is disproportionate. Declaration is explicit: - `@RunWith(RobolectricTestRunner::class)` on the class (JUnit4) or `@ExtendWith(RobolectricExtension::class)` (JUnit5 via `robolectric-junit5`). - `@Config(sdk = [34])` fixes the API level. Never use `@Config(sdk = [Config.NEWEST_SDK])` — silent version drift. - Robolectric tests still live in `src/test/**` (they are JVM tests), but the file name convention makes it obvious: `<Class>RobolectricTest.kt` or a `robolectric/` subdirectory. A reviewer scanning `src/test/**` should be able to tell in one glance which tests are pure-JVM and which touch Robolectric.

A module uses JUnit4 or JUnit5 — not both. Mixing runs both engines through Gradle's `useJUnitPlatform()`/`useJUnit()` dispatch and produces confusing failure attribution. JUnit5 is the default for greenfield modules (parameterized tests via `@ParameterizedTest`, nested classes via `@Nested`, dynamic tests). JUnit4 is retained only when the module depends on legacy runners (`AndroidJUnit4`, `MockitoJUnitRunner`) that lack a JUnit5 counterpart in the project's dependency set. Version choice is fixed at the module `build.gradle{.kts}` — no per-file switching.

Instrumented tests in `src/androidTest/**` use AndroidX Test — `androidx.test:runner`, `androidx.test:core`, `androidx.test.ext:junit`. The runner declaration is `@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4::class)` on the class. Legacy `android.test.*` and `android.support.test.*` are archived — new tests must NOT introduce them; old tests should migrate opportunistically when the file is touched.

File name matches the class under test with the `Test` suffix: `UserRepositoryTest.kt`, `UserRepositoryRobolectricTest.kt`, `UserRepositoryInstrumentedTest.kt`. One production class per test file (multi-class exceptions are pair-programming-obvious data-class bundles). Test method names use Kotlin's backtick-quoted syntax to spell scenarios in a readable form: `` `returns cached user when repository is warm`() ``. Backticks are the JUnit5-compatible way to keep BDD-style scenario names in Kotlin without a separate DSL.

BDD scenarios from the task ticket §4 map to test methods with a 1:1 correspondence — either through the `` `<scenario-name>`() `` backtick convention (JUnit5) or through `@DisplayName("<scenario-name>")` on a conventionally named method (JUnit4/JUnit5). This makes ticket §4 → test-file traceability mechanical: `grep <scenario-name>` finds the test.

`@Before` / `@BeforeEach` sets up fixtures. It MUST NOT mutate shared static state, MUST NOT hit the network, MUST NOT open files outside `@TempDir` (JUnit5) / `TemporaryFolder` (JUnit4). Fixture factories are the default; per-case builders live inside the case, not in a shared field, unless the field is `val` and immutable. See `testing-common` for the general rule; Android-specific reinforcement: shared `Context`/`Application` instances are a common leak vector — obtain via `ApplicationProvider.getApplicationContext()` (Robolectric) per test, not stashed in a companion object.

All `testing-common` discipline applies unchanged: unified context per file, factory-over-hooks, file-size budget, snapshot-operator-confirm, no auto-mocking framework classes without operator sign-off. This directive only adds Android-specific overlays — it does NOT relax inherited rules.

Definitions.Definition: A JUnit4/JUnit5 test under `src/test/**` executed on the developer's JVM via `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`. Pure Kotlin/Java; no Android framework unless Robolectric is explicitly opted in.

A test under `src/androidTest/**` executed on a real device or emulator via `./gradlew connectedAndroidTest`. Uses AndroidX Test; `@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4::class)`. Excluded from `gennady verify` base plan.

A local JVM test that uses the Robolectric runner to obtain shadowed Android framework classes without a device. Still lives under `src/test/**`; opt-in via `@RunWith(RobolectricTestRunner::class)` and `@Config(sdk = [N])`.

Pattern.Intent: Baseline local unit test — JUnit5, no Android framework, backtick scenario name.

Bad.reason: Mocks android.content.Context in a local test — lies about the runtime (AX_ANDROID_TEST_LOCAL_NO_FRAMEWORK).

Pattern.Intent: Local JVM test that legitimately needs Android framework — opt into Robolectric with explicit SDK.
Instrumented test in the correct source set — AndroidX Test, out of the verify loop.

AndroidTestingRules.SelfCheck: Before marking any Android test file done: 1. File is in the correct source set (`src/test/**` for JVM, `src/androidTest/**` for device). 2. Local JVM tests import no `android.*` classes unless Robolectric is opted in with explicit `@Config(sdk = [N])`. 3. Test class uses one JUnit version (4 or 5), matching the module's `build.gradle{.kts}`. 4. Test methods spell scenarios via backticks or `@DisplayName` — reviewable against ticket §4 by grep. 5. No mocking of Android framework classes in local unit tests. 6. Instrumented tests use `@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4::class)` and AndroidX Test primitives. 7. Robolectric tests declare explicit `@Config(sdk = [N])`, not `NEWEST_SDK`. 8. `testing-common` axioms (unified context, factory-over-hooks, file budget) hold.
